newsitem.title: CAYMAN ISLANDS: Swiss couple wins court case in Caymans.
newsitem.headline: Swiss couple wins court case in Caymans.

text.p: Swiss nationals Peter and Barbara Kruger, who are wanted in their homeland on charges of filing a false bankruptcy for $272 million, won a court case in the Cayman Islands on Wednesday.

Judge J. David Murphy dismissed the Swiss government's request for materials and documents that were seized by Cayman police in February 1996 when the Krugers were first taken into custody on an extradition warrant.

The Krugers in August had defeated an extradition order that would have sent them back to Switzerland to face charges. In the recent hearing, they claimed the documents were illegally seized during a search of their house and should not be handed over to Swiss authorities.
Murphy agreed, noting that the extradition law between the United Kingdom and Switzerland is more than 100 years old and should be updated.

He also ordered that the Cayman Islands legal department, which represented the Swiss government, pay legal costs. And he called the application for the documents by the Swiss government an "abuse of this court's process."

The Swiss government has claimed that the Krugers, who have permanent residency in the Cayman Islands, filed a false bankruptcy in Switzerland while hiding more than $10 million in assets in the Cayman Islands alone, as well as a chalet in France, a beachfront home in Florida, tennis club and private airplane in Canada.
Several major Swiss banks and some local institutions lost millions when the Kruger's real estate empire in Switzerland collapsed in the early 1990s and they filed for bankruptcy.
